papers.title: Advances in Key Genetic Elements and Strategies for High-Yield Heterologous Protein Expression in <i>Komagataella phaffii</i>.
papers.summary: This review describes engineered Komagataella phaffii expression systems for improving recombinant protein production through promoter, signal peptide, molecular chaperone, ER folding, unfolded protein response, and secretory-pathway optimization. It does not study Pompe disease, GAA, or the specific mechanism of GAA maturation, so the findings are transferable only as general strategies for improving protein folding and maturation in heterologous protein expression systems.

papers.title: The N-terminal domain of the endoplasmic reticulum-resident chaperone Grp94 functions in aggregation prevention.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the N-terminal domain of the endoplasmic-reticulum chaperone Grp94 suppresses aggregation of model client proteins independently of ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis, and calcium binding. The isolated N-terminal domain is sufficient for aggregation suppression, whereas full-length Grp94 is required for efficient downstream client release and BiP-mediated reactivation; the H146D mutant improves aggregation suppression at limiting chaperone concentrations but impairs luciferase reactivation.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of the impact of Heat shock protein 90 kDa or Cdc37 mutation on the yeast proteome.
papers.summary: This study uses yeast mutants affecting Hsp90 or its cochaperone Cdc37 to examine protein-client loading, folding-cycle stages, and proteome-wide effects. Cdc37-S14A and the Hsp90 loading-step mutant Hsc82-G309S produced similar changes in soluble protein abundance, including effects on multiple protein kinases and additional non-kinase proteins. The work provides a transferable experimental and proteomic framework for studying chaperone-dependent protein maturation, but it does not directly study GAA or Pompe disease.

papers.title: Binding of 3,4,5,6-tetrahydroxyazepanes to the acid-β-glucosidase active site: implications for pharmacological chaperone design for Gaucher disease.
papers.summary: This study shows that 3,4,5,6-tetrahydroxyazepane compounds can bind and stabilize mutant acid-β-glucosidase (GCase), with the core azepane compound 1 modestly increasing GCase activity in patient-derived Gaucher disease fibroblasts. Thermal stabilization was not sufficient by itself to predict cellular chaperoning activity, and compounds 2 and 3 did not improve mutant GCase activity in the tested fibroblast models.

papers.title: Optimizing protein folding in prokaryotes: Strategies to enhance soluble expression of recombinant proteins.
papers.summary: This review describes intrinsic molecular redesign and extrinsic folding modulation as complementary strategies for improving correct folding and soluble expression of recombinant proteins in prokaryotic systems. It also identifies artificial intelligence-driven folding prediction and high-throughput screening as forward-looking tools, but reports no data on GAA maturation or Pompe disease.

papers.title: Oral pharmacological chaperone migalastat compared with enzyme replacement therapy in Fabry disease: 18-month results from the randomised phase III ATTRACT study.
papers.summary: In an 18-month randomised phase III study, oral migalastat stabilised mutant lysosomal α-galactosidase and promoted its lysosomal trafficking in patients with Fabry disease and amenable GLA mutations. Migalastat maintained renal function and low plasma lyso-Gb3 comparably to enzyme replacement therapy while significantly decreasing left ventricular mass index.

papers.title: Cellular and biochemical response to chaperone versus substrate reduction therapies in neuropathic Gaucher disease.
papers.summary: In patient-derived GD2-3 fibroblasts, PBMC, and macrophages, ambroxol and eliglustat increased glucocerebrosidase activity, glucocerebrosidase–LAMP1 colocalization, lysosomal activity, autophagy-related readouts, and mitochondrial function. The study demonstrates transferable small-molecule strategies for improving lysosomal enzyme trafficking and downstream lysosomal dynamics, although responses of glucocerebrosidase activity were GBA-variant-dependent and high concentrations reduced cell viability and ATP levels.

papers.title: Structure of acid beta-glucosidase with pharmacological chaperone provides insight into Gaucher disease.
papers.summary: This paper reports that isofagomine (IFG) binds the active site of acid beta-glucosidase (GCase), increases GCase activity in cell lysates, and restores lysosomal trafficking in cells carrying the N370S mutant GCase associated with Gaucher disease. Structural comparisons indicate that IFG induces an active GCase conformation stabilized by interactions involving Asn370, supporting stabilization of substrate-bound conformations as a therapeutic strategy for protein misfolding and mistrafficking.

papers.title: The pharmacological chaperone isofagomine increases the activity of the Gaucher disease L444P mutant form of beta-glucosidase.
papers.summary: Isofagomine acted as a pharmacological chaperone for mutant L444P acid β-glucosidase, increasing its lysosomal trafficking, cellular and tissue activity, and, after washout, reducing endogenous glucosylceramide in Gaucher patient-derived cells. Oral treatment also increased GCase activity across mouse tissues and reduced selected Gaucher-associated markers, but the paper does not study rhGAA or establish transfer to lysosomal targeting of rhGAA in glycogen storage disease II.

papers.title: pH-Responsive Trihydroxylated Piperidines Rescue The Glucocerebrosidase Activity in Human Fibroblasts Bearing The Neuronopathic Gaucher-Related L444P/L444P Mutations in GBA1 Gene.
papers.summary: The paper reports stereoselective preparation and testing of a pH-responsive, orthoester-appended trihydroxylated piperidine iminosugar as a pharmacological chaperone for mutant glucocerebrosidase (GCase). In human fibroblasts carrying the neuronopathic Gaucher-associated GBA1 L444P/L444P mutation, the compound increased lysosomal GCase activity, whereas stability testing showed loss of inhibitory activity over time in acidic medium.

papers.title: Immune tolerance induction for laronidase treatment in mucopolysaccharidosis I.
papers.summary: A small Phase 2 trial found that prophylactic cyclosporine plus azathioprine with low-dose laronidase induced the protocol-defined immune-tolerance response in one evaluable patient with severe MPS I, but not in the other patients; the study was terminated early with inconclusive results. The paper also reviews immune-modulation regimens used in Pompe disease that suppress anti-drug antibodies and may improve enzyme replacement therapy responses in other lysosomal storage disorders.

papers.title: Immune Modulation for Enzyme Replacement Therapy in A Female Patient With Hunter Syndrome.
papers.summary: In a 3.5-year-old girl with severe mucopolysaccharidosis type II, concurrent immune tolerance induction with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin was associated with very low anti-idursulfase antibody titers, clinical stability, and no significant infusion-related adverse effects. The protocol was adapted from reports in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease, supporting potential transfer to patients with other lysosomal storage disorders receiving enzyme replacement therapy.

papers.title: Anti-drug antibody formation in Japanese Fabry patients following enzyme replacement therapy.
papers.summary: In 97 Japanese patients with Fabry disease receiving enzyme replacement therapy, anti-α-Gal IgG antibodies developed mainly in classic Fabry males, were usually neutralizing, and impaired the treatment-associated reduction of plasma lyso-Gb3. Two antibody-positive patients acquired apparent immune tolerance during continued therapy, while an immunochromatographic assay correlated with ELISA and was proposed as a rapid bedside antibody test.

papers.title: Rescue immune tolerance induction with a recombinant factor Fc-fused VIII: prospective ReITIrate study of clinical, humoral and cellular immune responses.
papers.summary: In this prospective, single-arm study of rescue immune tolerance induction with efmoroctocog alfa in 16 patients with severe haemophilia A and previous induction failure, four achieved negative inhibitor titres and one met all stringent success criteria within 60 weeks. Immunophenotyping showed an increase in regulatory T cells, supporting the concept that immune tolerance to enzyme replacement therapy can be promoted and measured, although complete success was uncommon and the findings require confirmation.

papers.title: Anti-BlyS antibody reduces the immune reaction against enzyme and enhances the efficacy of enzyme replacement therapy in Fabry disease model mice.
papers.summary: In Fabry disease model mice, belimumab (anti-BlyS antibody) reduced B cells and antibodies against recombinant human GLA, and higher maintenance dosing induced immune tolerance in 50% of mice. High-dose belimumab also improved therapeutic enzyme distribution and clearance of GL-3, but antibody formation was not completely prevented.

papers.title: Synthetic immunomodulation with a CRISPR super-repressor in vivo.
papers.summary: The paper shows that an AAV-delivered CRISPR transcriptional super-repressor targeting MYD88 can transiently suppress antiviral humoral immunity, including antibodies against AAV capsids and transgene cargo, thereby improving the efficiency of subsequent AAV9-mediated PCSK9 repression. Pretreatment with the MYD88 repressor also reduced inflammatory responses and tissue-injury markers in mouse models of LPS-induced septicemia, while long-term monitoring found no significant changes in measured major-organ function markers.

papers.title: Antisense Oligonucleotide-Based Rescue of Aberrant Splicing Defects Caused by 15 Pathogenic Variants in ABCA4.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that 2′-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides can redirect cryptic or aberrant splicing caused by 15 pathogenic ABCA4 intronic variants in a HEK293T midigene assay, with correction reported for 14 variants. Correction was variant- and target-dependent, including complete correction of multiple pseudoexon-inclusion defects but no correction of the c.3191-11T>A exon-elongation defect, supporting transfer of AON-based cryptic-splicing modulation to GAA splice-associated disease mechanisms without demonstrating application to Pompe disease.

papers.title: Consensus guidelines for assessing eligibility of pathogenic DNA variants for antisense oligonucleotide treatments.
papers.summary: This paper presents and validates the N1C VARIANT consensus guidelines for assessing whether pathogenic DNA variants may be eligible for antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) treatment. The guidelines cover splice correction, exon skipping, transcript knockdown, and wild-type allele upregulation, and provide a calculator, training videos, and publicly available resources to support variant assessment. The paper does not report experimental rescue of a specific disease variant or directly study GAA or Pompe disease.

papers.title: Targeted antisense oligonucleotide treatment rescues developmental alterations in spinal muscular atrophy organoids.
papers.summary: In patient-derived SMA spinal cord organoids, SMN deficiency altered pre-mRNA splicing and early neuronal development, while an SMN2-targeting r6-morpholino restored full-length SMN, corrected thousands of splicing events, and rescued cellular and electrophysiological defects. The paper does not describe the process as “cryptic splicing”; instead, it reports aberrant alternative splicing and exon skipping, making this an indirect mechanistic precedent for testing splice-correction strategies in splice-associated GAA disease.

papers.title: Synergistic Effect of an Antisense Oligonucleotide and Small Molecule on Splicing Correction of the Spinal Muscular Atrophy Gene.
papers.summary: In GM03813 spinal muscular atrophy patient fibroblasts, low-dose combinations of the ISS-N1-targeting antisense oligonucleotide Anti-N1 with risdiplam or branaplam produced synergistic correction of SMN2 exon 7 splicing. RNA-Seq indicated that these low-dose combinations retained relatively limited transcriptomic perturbations and showed little or no additive off-target effects compared with individual treatments.

papers.title: A splice-switching oligonucleotide treatment ameliorates glycogen storage disease type 1a in mice with G6PC c.648G>T.
papers.summary: This paper shows that the GalNAc-conjugated splice-switching oligonucleotide DS-4108b redirects G6PC c.648G>T aberrant splicing in human 293A cells and a knock-in mouse model of glycogen storage disease type 1a, restoring hepatic G6Pase activity and improving fasting hypoglycemia and hepatic abnormalities. The effect was predominantly hepatic, with no clear correction of aberrant splicing, nephromegaly, or renal histology after 20 weeks.

papers.title: Tailored antisense oligonucleotides designed to correct aberrant splicing reveal actionable groups of mutations for rare genetic disorders.
papers.summary: The study developed tailored antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) to correct five mutation-associated patterns of aberrant splicing in HEK293 minigene models, including activation of cryptic exons. PMO, Vivo-morpholino, and 2′-O-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate chemistries showed mutation- and transcript-specific rescue, with toxicity and incomplete correction in some cases.

papers.title: Evaluation of oxidative stress and mitochondrial function in a type II mucopolysaccharidosis cellular model: in vitro effects of genistein and coenzyme Q10.
papers.summary: The paper shows that IDS-deficient HEK 293 cellular models of mucopolysaccharidosis type II exhibit increased reactive species production, increased antioxidant enzyme activities, increased lysosomal volume, and oxidative DNA damage, without evidence of altered mitochondrial function. Genistein and coenzyme Q10 showed antioxidant protective effects in vitro by reducing reactive species production, superoxide dismutase activity, or DNA damage at the tested concentrations.

papers.title: Tumour suppressor SIRT3 deacetylates and activates manganese superoxide dismutase to scavenge ROS.
papers.summary: The paper shows that oxidative stress induces SIRT3, which deacetylates mitochondrial SOD2 at K68 and increases its antioxidant activity. SIRT3-dependent SOD2 activation lowers mitochondrial and cellular reactive oxygen species, while SIRT3 depletion, K68-acetylation, or SOD2 depletion increases reactive oxygen species.

papers.title: Impaired ROS Scavenging System in Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Generated from Patients with MERRF Syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper establishes patient-derived MERRF hiPSCs carrying the mitochondrial DNA A8344G mutation as in vitro models that exhibit elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS), impaired mitochondrial respiration, and fragmented mitochondria. The same ROS and mitochondrial abnormalities persist in differentiated cardiomyocyte-like cells and neural progenitor cells, while prior work cited by the paper reports that co-enzyme Q10 decreases ROS and eliminates mitochondrial dysfunction in A8344G-containing cells.

papers.title: DPP-4 enzyme deficiency protects kidney from acute ischemia-reperfusion injury: role for remote intermittent bowel ischemia-reperfusion preconditioning.
papers.summary: In a rat model of acute kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury, DPP4 deficiency and remote small-bowel ischemia-reperfusion preconditioning increased circulating GLP-1 and antioxidant proteins, reduced oxidative stress and kidney damage, and preserved renal function and architecture. The paper measured oxidative stress using oxidized-protein oxyblotting, H2DCFDA-detectable reactive oxygen species, and antioxidant-protein expression, but did not test these interventions in Pompe disease.

papers.title: Linoleic Acid Attenuates Denervation-Induced Skeletal Muscle Atrophy in Mice through Regulation of Reactive Oxygen Species-Dependent Signaling.
papers.summary: Linoleic acid protected H2O2-stressed C2C12 myoblasts from oxidative stress, apoptosis, and induction of muscle-atrophy genes, while restoring skeletal-muscle volume and selected protein levels in sciatic-denervated C57BL/6 mice. The study therefore identifies linoleic acid as a mechanistically relevant antioxidant intervention for oxidative-stress-associated muscle atrophy, although it was not tested in glycogen storage disease II.

papers.title: Pleurotus albidus Modulates Mitochondrial Metabolism Disrupted by Hyperglycaemia in EA.hy926 Endothelial Cells.
papers.summary: The study shows that Pleurotus albidus extract (PleExt), a source of phenolic compounds and ergothioneine, reduced hyperglycaemia-associated reactive oxygen species, lipid and protein oxidative damage, antioxidant enzyme imbalance, and nitric oxide depletion in EA.hy926 endothelial cells. The extract also prevented the hyperglycaemia-associated increase in mitochondrial electron-transport-chain complex I activity, but the responsible compounds and possible SIRT3 involvement remain unconfirmed.

unread.title: Correction of oxidative stress enhances enzyme replacement therapy in Pompe disease.
unread.why: Demonstrates experimentally that antioxidant correction enhances recombinant human GAA activity and treatment effects in Pompe cells and mice.

unread.title: Unusual Evolution of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Non-Compaction Myocardium in a Pompe Disease Patient.
unread.why: Reports use of cipaglucosidase alfa with miglustat and documents improved cardiac hypertrophy with a distinctive cardiac remodeling outcome.

unread.title: Improved Enzyme Replacement Therapy with Cipaglucosidase Alfa/Miglustat in Infantile Pompe Disease.
unread.why: Provides patient-level evidence that switching to cipaglucosidase alfa/miglustat improves respiratory, cardiac, and motor outcomes in infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Detection of gene variants associated with recessive limb-girdle muscular weakness and Pompe disease in a global cohort of patients through the application of next-generation sequencing analysis.
unread.why: Validates a scalable NGS approach that identified Pompe disease among 2,372 patients with limb-girdle muscular weakness.

unread.title: A favorable outcome in an infantile-onset Pompe patient with cross reactive immunological material (CRIM) negative disease with high dose enzyme replacement therapy and adjusted immunomodulation.
unread.why: Reports a successful high-dose ERT plus immunomodulation strategy in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease with immune-tolerance and clinical outcomes.

unread.title: Development of high sustained anti-drug antibody titers and corresponding clinical decline in a late-onset Pompe disease patient after 11+ years on enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: Demonstrates that antibody and biomarker surveillance can identify ERT failure and that immunomodulation can restore clinical and biomarker outcomes.

unread.title: Assessment of the functional impact on the pre-mRNA splicing process of 28 nucleotide variants associated with Pompe disease in GAA exon 2 and their recovery using antisense technology.
unread.why: Shows experimentally that antisense oligonucleotides rescue GAA splicing defects caused by multiple Pompe disease variants.

unread.title: Molecular Diagnosis of Pompe Disease in the Genomic Era: Correlation with Acid Alpha-Glucosidase Activity in Dried Blood Spots.
unread.why: The study validates a combined gene-panel and dried-blood-spot enzymatic workflow for diagnosing Pompe disease while identifying pseudodeficiency and analytically ambiguous cases.

unread.title: Extensive digital health technology assessment detects subtle motor impairment in mild and asymptomatic Pompe disease.
unread.why: Digital mobility testing detected subtle movement abnormalities in mildly affected or asymptomatic Pompe patients despite normal conventional clinical scores.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation and CRIM status in Vietnamese children with Pompe disease: a single-center experience.
unread.why: The cohort provides GAA genotype, CRIM status, and clinical-outcome data supporting CRIM testing and comprehensive genotyping for prognosis and therapeutic decisions.

unread.title: Pompe disease: early diagnosis and early treatment make a difference.
unread.why: The review describes established diagnostic and treatment approaches and reports that early alglucosidase alfa therapy improves survival, motor development, and cardiac outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical insight meets scientific innovation to develop a next generation ERT for Pompe disease.
unread.why: The paper describes the development and clinical rationale for avalglucosidase alfa as a next-generation ERT for Pompe disease while detailing the limitations of first-generation ERT.

unread.title: Umbilical Cord Blood Sampling for Newborn Screening of Pompe Disease and the Detection of a Novel Pathogenic Variant and Pseudodeficiency Variants in an Asian Population.
unread.why: Analysis of 4,091 cord-blood specimens supports UCB GAA measurement by UPLC-MS/MS as a viable newborn-screening alternative and identifies confirmatory variants.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy during pregnancy and breastfeeding in late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The case series provides direct evidence that continuing alglucosidase alfa during pregnancy and breastfeeding was feasible, safe, and compatible with normal child growth and development.

unread.title: Identification of the first deletion-insertion involving the complete structure of GAA gene and part of CCDC40 gene mediated by an Alu element.
unread.why: The report identifies a complex GAA-CCDC40 deletion-insertion and demonstrates the need to include breakpoint-level analysis for large rearrangements in Pompe molecular diagnosis.

unread.title: Optimizing clinical outcomes: The journey of twins with CRIM-negative infantile-onset Pompe disease on high-dose enzyme replacement therapy and immunomodulation.
unread.why: The twins achieved antibody tolerance and cardiac and biomarker improvement with high-dose ERT combined with immune tolerance induction, while later switching to avalglucosidase alfa.

unread.title: Molecular and functional characterization of eight novel GAA mutations in Italian infants with Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study experimentally and computationally characterizes eight pathogenic GAA variants and shows how molecular and functional testing can predict infantile Pompe severity.

unread.title: Mass Spectrometry but Not Fluorimetry Distinguishes Affected and Pseudodeficiency Patients in Newborn Screening for Pompe Disease.
unread.why: Direct comparison showed that tandem-MS analysis better separates Pompe disease from pseudodeficiency and carrier newborns than fluorimetry.

unread.title: Phenotypic implications of pathogenic variant types in Pompe disease.
unread.why: Provides patient data showing that molecular variant patterns and combined clinical assessments can predict Pompe subtype and severity better than enzyme activity alone.

unread.title: The phenotype, genotype, and outcome of infantile-onset Pompe disease in 18 Saudi patients.
unread.why: Reports genotype and clinical outcomes from 18 infants treated with ERT and identifies early detection and immunomodulation as potentially actionable factors.

unread.title: Glycogen storage disease type II: enzymatic screening in dried blood spots on filter paper.
unread.why: Develops and validates a noninvasive newborn-screening assay that distinguishes Pompe patients from carriers and controls.

unread.title: Consensus treatment recommendations for late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: Provides a systematic, expert-derived treatment and management protocol for selecting, initiating, monitoring, and discontinuing ERT in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Update of the Pompe disease mutation database with 107 sequence variants and a format for severity rating.
unread.why: Expands a disease-specific GAA variant database and introduces a standardized severity-rating system for diagnosis and prognosis.

unread.title: Current status of newborn screening for Pompe disease in Japan.
unread.why: A Japanese newborn-screening study demonstrates feasibility of GAA activity testing and reports early diagnosis enabling prompt enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Six-Minute Walk Distance Is a Useful Outcome Measure to Detect Motor Decline in Treated Late-Onset Pompe Disease Patients.
unread.why: Longitudinal data in treated late-onset Pompe disease show that 6MWD detects motor decline when other performance tests do not change significantly.

unread.title: A rapid and non-invasive proteomic analysis using DBS and buccal swab for multiplexed second-tier screening of Pompe disease and Mucopolysaccharidosis type I.
unread.why: The study validates a rapid proteomic assay that quantifies endogenous GAA and distinguishes Pompe disease from pseudodeficiency and carrier states.

unread.title: Home-Based Infusion of Alglucosidase Alfa Can Safely be Implemented in Adults with Late-Onset Pompe Disease: Lessons Learned from 18,380 Infusions.
unread.why: Analysis of 18,380 infusions supports safe home administration of alglucosidase alfa in selected adults when appropriate infrastructure and clinical backup are available.

unread.title: Pompe disease: Unmet needs and emerging therapies.
unread.why: This review summarizes established and emerging Pompe disease treatments, including current ERT, combination ERT, tissue-targeted delivery, substrate reduction, and gene-restoration approaches.

unread.title: Development of a clinically validated in vitro functional assay to assess pathogenicity of novel GAA variants in patients with Pompe disease identified via newborn screening.
unread.why: The authors validate a functional assay for assessing pathogenicity of novel GAA variants and apply it to classify variants found through newborn screening.

unread.title: High-risk screening of late-onset Pompe disease: A different early portrait in China.
unread.why: A multicenter prospective study validates high-risk DBS screening and molecular confirmation for late-onset Pompe disease in patients with respiratory insufficiency, weakness, or hyperCKemia.

unread.title: Investigating Late-Onset Pompe Prevalence in Neuromuscular Medicine Academic Practices: The IPaNeMA Study.
unread.why: The study evaluates a two-step enzyme and molecular testing strategy and documents a reusable multicenter patient dataset for late-onset Pompe disease detection.

unread.title: Immunophenotype associated with high sustained antibody titers against enzyme replacement therapy in infantile-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study identifies an immune signature and biomarker score associated with high sustained antibody titers that may compromise alglucosidase alfa therapy.

unread.title: Correlation of GAA Genotype and Acid-α-Glucosidase Enzyme Activity in Hungarian Patients with Pompe Disease.
unread.why: The study combines enzymatic and genetic testing in Pompe disease and relates GAA variants to residual enzyme activity and potential disease severity.

unread.title: Bioimpedance Phase Angle as a Prognostic Tool in Late-Onset Pompe Disease: A Single-Centre Prospective Study With a 15-year Follow-Up.
unread.why: A 15-year prospective study supports phase angle as a low-cost prognostic marker of muscle quality and long-term response to ERT in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Therapeutic thoroughfares for adults living with Pompe disease.
unread.why: Reviews phase 3, long-term, and clinical-trial evidence for multiple disease-modifying therapies in adult Pompe disease.

unread.title: Function, structure and quality of striated muscles in the lower extremities in patients with late onset Pompe Disease-an MRI study.
unread.why: Provides patient data validating quantitative MRI measures and clinical endpoints for monitoring treated late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation of 17 cases of Pompe disease in Spanish patients and identification of 4 novel GAA variants.
unread.why: Reports diagnostic testing and identification of four novel pathogenic GAA variants with genotype-phenotype data in Pompe disease.

unread.title: Two Approaches for a Genetic Analysis of Pompe Disease: A Literature Review of Patients with Pompe Disease and Analysis Based on Genomic Data from the General Population.
unread.why: Applies comparative genomic analysis to identify GAA variants, estimate carrier frequency, and predict Pompe disease prevalence in East Asian populations.

unread.title: Screening data from 19 patients with late-onset Pompe disease for a phase I clinical trial of AAV8 vector-mediated gene therapy.
unread.why: Provides Pompe-specific screening data and clinical and biomarker criteria for eligibility in an AAV8-GAA gene therapy trial.

unread.title: Base editing rescues acid α-glucosidase function in infantile-onset Pompe disease patient-derived cells.
unread.why: Demonstrates correction of three pathogenic GAA variants, restoration of enzyme activity, and reduced lysosomal burden in infantile-Pompe patient cells.

unread.title: The frequency of Duchenne muscular dystrophy/Becker muscular dystrophy and Pompe disease in children with isolated transaminase elevation: results from the observational VICTORIA study.
unread.why: Validates a practical screening pathway for detecting undiagnosed Pompe disease among children with persistent isolated transaminase elevation.

unread.title: Pompe disease: a country-wide molecular screening in a cohort of 15,068 study participants.
unread.why: Reports a country-scale molecular screening strategy that identified Pompe cases and 25 previously undescribed GAA variants.

unread.title: Diagnosis, management and monitoring of patients with Pompe disease in the UK.
unread.why: Provides the first UK-specific consensus guideline for diagnosing, monitoring, and managing Pompe disease.

unread.title: Dermatomyositis masking late onset Pompe disease in a patient with proximal muscle weakness.
unread.why: The case provides a concrete diagnostic workup and longitudinal clinical response data for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Can Alpha-Glucosidase Activity in Plasma or Leukocytes Serve as a Biomarker for Future Gene Therapy in Classic Infantile Pompe Disease?
unread.why: The study experimentally evaluates plasma and leukocyte GAA activity as pharmacokinetic and potential gene-therapy efficacy biomarkers in classic infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Integrating enzyme assay and molecular genetic testing for early diagnosis of infantile-onset Pompe disease: A case report.
unread.why: The report demonstrates an integrated dried-blood-spot enzyme and molecular testing strategy for early diagnosis of infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Clinical, pathological and genetic features as well as follow-up of 68 patients with late-onset Pompe disease: a single-center retrospective study.
unread.why: A 68-patient cohort provides real-world data on ERT, early initiation, functional outcomes, survival, and a candidate muscle pathology marker in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Physical therapy management of Pompe disease.
unread.why: The review describes reusable physical-therapy strategies for preserving mobility and managing motor dysfunction in Pompe disease alongside ERT.

unread.title: Clinical guidelines for late-onset Pompe disease.
unread.why: The guideline provides practical diagnostic confirmation and early ERT recommendations for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Fractures in children with Pompe disease: a potential long-term complication.
unread.why: The study identifies fractures as an adverse outcome associated with prolonged survival during ERT and supports vigilance and radiographic surveillance.

unread.title: Intracellular Membrane Repair Dysregulation and Accumulation of Mature Myostatin Protein are Novel Markers of Muscle Pathophysiology in Pompe Disease
unread.why: Longitudinal mouse analyses and patient biopsies identify membrane-repair proteins and myostatin dysregulation as measurable markers of Pompe muscle pathophysiology.

unread.title: A Genome Engineered Human Embryonic Stem Cell line to Investigate Pompe Disease
unread.why: The engineered human stem-cell model reproduces reduced GAA activity and disease-relevant lysosomal and glycogen phenotypes for scalable modeling and therapeutic screening.

unread.title: Umbilical Cord Blood Sampling for Newborn Screening of Pompe Disease and the Detection of a Novel Pathogenic Variant and Pseudodeficiency Variants in an Asian population
unread.why: A 4,091-infant screening study validates cord-blood GAA measurement and sequence confirmation as a feasible newborn-screening approach for Pompe disease.

unread.title: The Effect of Anti-drug Antibodies on the Bioavailability of Alglucosidase Alfa in Classic Infantile Pompe Disease.
unread.why: Patient pharmacokinetic and fibroblast studies show how anti-drug antibody testing and functional uptake assays can characterize and manage reduced alglucosidase bioavailability.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation in adult-onset acid maltase deficiency.
unread.why: The 16-patient study provides data supporting enzyme and creatine kinase testing for diagnosis and respiratory-function monitoring, while showing that these measures lack prognostic value.

unread.title: Muscular MRI-based algorithm to differentiate inherited myopathies presenting with spinal rigidity.
unread.why: The multicenter study developed and externally validated a whole-body MRI algorithm that differentiated inherited myopathies, including Pompe disease, presenting with spinal rigidity.

unread.title: 1,6-epi-Cyclophellitol Cyclosulfamidate Is a Bona Fide Lysosomal α-Glucosidase Stabilizer for the Treatment of Pompe Disease.
unread.why: The study showed that cyclosulfamidate 4 selectively stabilizes recombinant human GAA and facilitates its lysosomal delivery in vitro, in cells, and in zebrafish.

unread.title: Pompe disease ascertained through The Lantern Project, 2018-2021: Next-generation sequencing and enzymatic testing to overcome obstacles to diagnosis.
unread.why: The diagnostic program demonstrated in 140 confirmed Pompe cases that combined enzyme testing, targeted sequencing, and multigene next-generation sequencing facilitates accurate diagnosis.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy and immunotherapy lead to significant functional improvement in two children with Pompe disease: a case report.
unread.why: Two children with anti-GAA antibodies showed reduced antibody titers and functional improvement after methotrexate was added to enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Sensory neuropathy in patients with Pompe disease: a case series in Iran.
unread.why: The study validated a multimodal screening approach and identified previously unrecognized small- and large-fiber neuropathy in asymptomatic Pompe patients.

unread.title: Efficacy and safety of avalglucosidase alfa in Japanese patients with late-onset and infantile-onset Pompe diseases: A case series from clinical trials.
unread.why: Individual patient data from COMET and Mini-COMET support the efficacy and tolerability of avalglucosidase alfa in Japanese patients with late-onset or infantile-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: When the Diaphragm Fails: Visual Hallucinations Due to Isolated Respiratory Muscle Weakness as a First Manifestation of Late-Onset Pompe Disease.
unread.why: The case demonstrates an actionable diagnostic pathway using GAA testing and diaphragm-function assessment, followed by ventilatory support and disease-specific enzyme therapy.

unread.title: Clinical outcomes after long-term treatment with alglucosidase alfa in infants and children with advanced Pompe disease.
unread.why: The multicenter longitudinal trial showed that biweekly alglucosidase alfa improved survival, ventilation-free survival, cardiomyopathy, motor function, and independence in children with advanced Pompe disease.

unread.title: The impact of antibodies on clinical outcomes in diseases treated with therapeutic protein: lessons learned from infantile Pompe disease.
unread.why: Infantile Pompe data identify sustained high anti-rhGAA titers as a predictor of poor enzyme-replacement response and validate measurable response-monitoring endpoints.

unread.title: Early detection of Pompe disease by newborn screening is feasible: results from the Taiwan screening program.
unread.why: A large Taiwan program showed that dried-blood-spot enzyme testing can feasibly detect Pompe disease and enable earlier diagnosis and treatment.

unread.title: Survival and long-term outcomes in late-onset Pompe disease following alglucosidase alfa treatment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
unread.why: Meta-analysis provides quantitative evidence that alglucosidase alfa improves survival and motor and respiratory outcomes in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Successful immune tolerance induction to enzyme replacement therapy in CRIM-negative infantile Pompe disease.
unread.why: Four CRIM-negative infants achieved sustained immune tolerance and clinical benefit using rituximab and methotrexate with or without IVIG during enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Neural deficits contribute to respiratory insufficiency in Pompe disease.
unread.why: The study validates two Pompe animal models and identifies phrenic motor-neuron dysfunction as a respiratory target that muscle-only therapy may not address.

unread.title: Evasion of immune responses to introduced human acid alpha-glucosidase by liver-restricted expression in glycogen storage disease type II.
unread.why: Liver-restricted AAV8 GAA delivery increased tissue GAA, normalized muscle glycogen, and evaded humoral and cellular immune responses in Pompe mice.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of avalglucosidase alfa versus alglucosidase alfa in patients with late-onset Pompe disease (COMET): a phase 3, randomised, multicentre trial.
unread.why: The randomized phase 3 COMET trial showed that avalglucosidase alfa is noninferior to alglucosidase alfa and provides an effective approved enzyme-replacement option for late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy in late-onset Pompe disease: a systematic literature review.
unread.why: Systematic evidence from 368 late-onset Pompe patients indicates that alglucosidase alfa stabilizes or improves muscle and respiratory function and is generally well tolerated.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of recombinant acid alpha-glucosidase (rhGAA) in patients with classical infantile Pompe disease: results of a phase II clinical trial.
unread.why: Early clinical data show that weekly recombinant GAA improves cardiac, skeletal-muscle, respiratory, histologic, and biochemical disease measures in classic infantile Pompe disease.

unread.title: Pompe disease: design, methodology, and early findings from the Pompe Registry.
unread.why: The international Pompe Registry provides a large longitudinal resource for understanding phenotype, prognosis, treatment exposure, and natural disease course.

unread.title: Enzyme therapy for pompe disease with recombinant human alpha-glucosidase from rabbit milk.
unread.why: Four infants receiving recombinant rabbit-milk GAA achieved normalized muscle enzyme activity, reduced glycogen deposits, and clinical and cardiac improvement.

unread.title: Observational clinical study in juvenile-adult glycogenosis type 2 patients undergoing enzyme replacement therapy for up to 4 years.
unread.why: This multicenter study reports long-term alglucosidase alfa treatment outcomes and clinically usable functional, respiratory, cardiac, and biochemical measures in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of cipaglucosidase alfa plus miglustat versus alglucosidase alfa plus placebo in late-onset Pompe disease (PROPEL): an international, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
unread.why: This phase 3 trial directly tests a two-component enzyme-stabilizing therapy against alglucosidase alfa in late-onset Pompe disease.

unread.title: Correction of glycogen storage disease type II by an adeno-associated virus vector containing a muscle-specific promoter.
unread.why: The study demonstrates muscle- and cardiac-directed AAV GAA gene delivery that reduces glycogen accumulation in GAA-deficient mice, directly testing a Pompe disease gene-therapy approach.

unread.title: The pharmacological chaperone 1-deoxynojirimycin increases the activity and lysosomal trafficking of multiple mutant forms of acid alpha-glucosidase.
unread.why: The study shows that 1-deoxynojirimycin increases activity, maturation, and lysosomal localization of multiple Pompe-causing GAA mutants in experimental systems.

unread.title: A chaperone enhances blood α-glucosidase activity in Pompe disease patients treated with enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: The study directly shows that N-butyldeoxynojirimycin increases circulating alpha-glucosidase activity when combined with enzyme replacement therapy in Pompe disease patients.

unread.title: Newborn screening for lysosomal storage disorders in hungary.
unread.why: The Hungarian newborn-screening program identifies Pompe disease using tandem MS/MS followed by retesting and genetic confirmation, providing a directly transferable diagnostic strategy.
